title: Split loader stages and introduce asynchronous weight-activation protocol
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Our current model loader is a single blocking pipeline that parses manifests, materializes weight shards into memory, and initializes the tokenizer synchronously. This design causes long tail cold-starts (observed 850-1200ms p95 on 8k sequence models) and makes incremental rollout of new weight formats risky. Goal: Split the loader into distinct stages (manifest/metadata discovery, compatibility/adapters, lazy weight activation, tokenizer soft-init) and add a lightweight asynchronous 'weight-activation protocol' that allows the serving runtime to start accepting requests against a model slot while heavier tensor pages are activated in the background. This ticket implements the core refactor, compatibility adapters for legacy .ckpt formats, and a temporary tokenizer stub pattern so runtime can begin KV-cache warmup before tokenizer full handshake completes.
acceptance_criteria: Loader is split into at least four explicit stages with clear interfaces: discover, adapt, activate, finalize
A 'weight-activation protocol' exists as an abstract interface with two implementations: immediate (current behavior) and async (new behavior)
Cold-start p95 for standard 8k tests reduced by >=35% in canary (baseline: 950ms -> target <=620ms)
Compatibility adapters can load legacy weight formats (.ckpt v1/v2) without requiring model conversion in 95% of cases
Tokenizer soft-init enables accepting first tokenized requests within 100ms of activation start; final tokenizer swap to be transparent to requesters
All changes behind runtime feature flag runtime.async_weight_activation with canary rollout control
Unit and integration tests added; integration perf harness shows regression-free behaviour on GPU cluster
Design doc and migration guide published and linkable from Console rollout page
tasks: Design and review: define stage interface contracts (discover/adapt/activate/finalize)
Implement lightweight tokenizer stub + hot-swap mechanism
Implement async weight-activation protocol and a thread-safe activation state machine
Add compatibility adapters for legacy checkpoint formats and a manifest version detector
Expose runtime feature flag and canary policy hooks in Console
Add telemetry: activation_duration, activation_errors, tokenizer_swap_time, cold_start_latency per model
Perf test across representative models: 7B, 13B, and 70B sequences with 2k and 8k seq lengths
Write migration guide + Confluence design doc + sample GH PR template for partner teams
risks: Activation race conditions causing partial weight reads if synchronization is not strict
Tokenizer stub could diverge in byte-level tokenization for edge cases leading to subtle output divergence
Compatibility adapter may fail silently for exotic custom sharding schemes, requiring a fallback to conversion
Metrics spike may be misinterpreted as production regressions during canary if dashboards not annotated
test_plan: Unit tests for stage transitions and activation state machine (simulate intermittent I/O)
Integration test: start model slot with async activation flag and ensure first token path responds within 100ms
Perf harness run: compare cold-start p50/p95/p99 across baseline and async activation on dev cluster
Chaos test: force partial shard failure mid-activation and verify graceful fallback to immediate activation or abort
End-to-end validation with QA prompts + log-diff to ensure tokenizer hot-swap produces identical token IDs
Load test at 1k rps against canary subset to validate autoscaler behavior with async activation in place
notes: We opted for an adaptable protocol rather than an opinionated streaming format because it allows incremental rollout and easier debugging. Trade-offs: the async path adds complexity to the activation state machine and requires stronger telemetry. We will gate the async activation default behind a canary and monitor tokenization fidelity metrics closely.
